name: Verdant-Axis

civilization.name: Threnn Concord
civilization.notes: A tidal-locked civilization concentrated along the terminator band; masters of canyon agriculture and geothermal power, recently expanding to orbital habitats.

description: Verdant-Axis turns one face forever toward its sun, and all life crowds the thousand-kilometer twilight band between eternal day and eternal night. There the Threnn Concord has carved terraced cities into canyon walls deep enough to hold their own weather, fed by geothermal fields that burn like furnaces at the valley floors. Beyond the band, day-side dunes glow white-hot and the night side gleams with glacier fields lit by auroras that never fade.

In the canyons the air is thick with green: hanging farms cascade down cliff faces in braided curtains, and the sound of falling water never stops. Evening comes not with sunset but with shadow-line crossing—the Concord's clocks mark it as the Crossing—and the whole civilization pauses as darkness pours up out of the night side. The geothermal vents smell faintly of sulfur and iron, a smell locals call home.

The Concord achieved orbit two generations ago and immediately fortified it: defense platforms ring the planet in numbers wildly disproportionate to any known threat, and the government will not discuss what they anticipate. Older ruins beneath the deepest canyon cities suggest the Threnn were not this world's first civilization—only its most recent—and whatever came before left no bones, only foundations.

First-contact protocols have been opened twice by passing traders; both times the platforms locked targeting solutions and the talks ended before they began. The Concord's biomass and medicinal compounds would transform three struggling colonies overnight, and everyone in the sector knows it. The question every intelligence service is asking is the same one the platforms seem built to answer: what does a civilization this young think it is defending against?
